title.purpose: Card and section titles, identity-band name.

label.purpose: Status badges, grouped-list section headers, tab labels.

shadows.name: floating-surface
shadows.purpose: A scrolling panel, bottom bar, or bubble stacked above/below a fixed sibling - never an ordinary card at rest.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: A numeric stat animates up into place on mount/change (rating, points) instead of appearing flat - the one authored motion moment, not scattered per-element effects.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one call-to-action color on a screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #2563eb; color: #ffffff; padding: 10px 18px; border-radius: 999px; border: none; font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; transition: opacity 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.92; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Bordered, neutral action - Cancel, Edit-adjacent actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #ffffff; color: #4b5563; padding: 10px 18px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid #d1d5db; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #f9fafb; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Soft-tint pill naming a state (resolved, pending, cancelled).
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 3px 9px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-badge-success { background: #f0fdf4; color: #15803d; } .ds-badge-warning { background: #fffbeb; color: #d97706; } .ds-badge-danger { background: #fef2f2; color: #dc2626; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The standard bordered, flat content container.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius: 16px; padding: 20px; } .ds-card-title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; color: #111827; margin-bottom: 12px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 14px; color: #111827; }

components.description: The signature settings-row unit: icon chip, label + caption, trailing accessory, stacked into one bordered container with hairline dividers between rows.

narrative.overview: Jageer Nepal reads as equipment you rely on, not a storefront you browse: confident, no-nonsense, built for getting a job done. One blue carries the whole brand - no secondary or tertiary accent competes with it - set against white surfaces and a soft gray canvas, separated by hairline borders rather than shadows. Type leans bold and heavy at every level except body copy; there is no ornamental serif, no display face, no gradient, nothing decorative standing between the visitor and the task. The system is the same across every role (client, technician, reseller, wholesaler, admin) and every platform it ships to (iOS, Android, web) - one shared toolbelt, not five branded apps wearing the same logo.
keyCharacteristics: One brand blue, no competing accent
Generous, consistent rounding (16px cards, full-round pills/avatars) - never a sharp corner
Flat-and-bordered by default; shadow is reserved for things that float above the page
Bold/extrabold type carries hierarchy; body copy stays regular weight
Soft-tint semantic badges (light background, saturated text) for every status

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Trusted Blue is the only saturated color that carries UI meaning (action, selection, identity). Status pairs are the sole exception, and they are always soft-tint, never solid-fill.

rules.name: The Soft Badge Rule
rules.body: A status is always a light-tint background with saturated text of the same hue family, rounded full, never a solid-fill chip.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Family Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a second font family for hierarchy or "brand feel." A heavier weight of the same system sans is always the right move.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A card or list row is separated from its neighbors by a 1px border, never a shadow. Shadow is earned only by an element that is actually stacked above other content.

dos: Do use Trusted Blue for the one thing on a screen that means "act" or "this is selected" - not for decoration.
Do separate cards, rows, and sections with borders/hairlines, not shadows.
Do reach for a grouped list (not repeated cards) once three or more simple rows would otherwise stack.
Do carry a soft-tint status pair whenever the product needs to say pending/success/danger.
Do draw icons from Ionicons only, one consistent outline/filled pairing for inactive/active state.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color; status pairs are the only sanctioned exception, and they stay soft-tint.
Don't use emoji as an icon substitute anywhere in the UI.
Don't add a shadow to an element that isn't actually floating above other content.
Don't introduce a display/serif font for "brand feel" - hierarchy comes from weight on the one system sans.
Don't use a solid-fill red (or any solid semantic color) for a status badge or destructive button; keep destructive actions as bordered white with red text.
